sourceName: National Forest dispersed camping / overnight pull-offs -- Eldorado NF (US-50 / Echo Summit) and Tahoe NF (I-80 / Donner Summit)
method: Hand research, 2026-08-12. Started from the official USDA Forest Service pages for Eldorado NF and Tahoe NF (camping, general rules, alerts/forest orders) and the California State Parks OHMVR SNO-PARK program pages, then read the governing forest orders themselves (Eldorado 03-25-08 camping occupancy, 03-26-05 fire restrictions, 03-26-01 Mormon Emigrant Trail winter closure; Tahoe 17-26-05 camping occupancy, 17-25-05 Truckee/Sierraville camping and campfire restrictions -- the last extracted from the signed PDF including its Appendix A legal area descriptions). Candidate named spots came from local/community sources (discoverechosummit.com, arounddonnersummit.com, The Dyrt) and were then checked against the official rules above. Community-sourced coordinates are marked verified:false. NOTE ON SCOPE: DESIGN.md defers public-land camping to phase 2 / icebox and the build script blocks the `blm` slug. This set uses its own slug, `dispersed-nf`, so it can be adopted or dropped whole. It is deliberately short -- see `gaps` below for what was researched and rejected, and why.
policyNote: READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANY PIN IN THIS FILE. These are public-land pins, not businesses: the rules are set by forest orders that are re-issued every one to three years and by fire restrictions that change within a single season. Everything below was true on 2026-08-12 and must be re-checked before a trip. ELDORADO NF (US-50 / Echo Summit): dispersed camping is free and allowed on most forest land unless specifically prohibited; campsites must be outside the boundary markings of developed campgrounds and at least 100 feet from streams and lakes; vehicles must stay on roads designated on the Motor Vehicle Use Map (MVUM) and be parked within one vehicle length of the edge of the road surface -- off-designated-route travel has been prohibited since the 2008 travel management decision (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/eldorado/recreation/camping-cabins). STAY LIMIT: Forest Order 03-25-08, effective 2025-10-17 through 2028-10-16, prohibits camping in any undeveloped location within one ranger district for more than 10 days per calendar year (14 days in a developed campground) (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/eldorado/alerts/camping-occupancy-restrictions). SEASONAL: all dirt roads and trails on the Eldorado are closed to motor vehicle use January 1 through March 31, and that closure may be extended while roads are wet. FIRE, CURRENT: Eldorado Forest Order 03-26-05, effective 2026-07-17 through 2026-11-29, prohibits building, maintaining, attending or using any fire, campfire or stove fire -- INCLUDING gas stoves and lanterns -- outside the developed recreation sites listed in its Exhibit A (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/eldorado/alerts/fire-restrictions-are-effect-forest-wide). That order does not prohibit camping or sleeping in a vehicle; it prohibits flame. Outside fire-restriction season, a free California Campfire Permit is required for any campfire, stove or lantern used outside a developed campground, valid January 1 to December 31 (https://www.preventwildfiresca.org). TAHOE NF (I-80 / Donner Summit): stay limit is 14 days per calendar year per ranger district for both dispersed and developed camping, Forest Order 17-26-05, effective 2026-04-05 through 2028-04-05 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/tahoe/alerts/14-day-camping-occupancy-restrictions-0). Forest Order 17-25-05, effective 2025-07-01 through 2028-06-30, prohibits BOTH camping and fires throughout named Restricted Use Areas in the Truckee and Sierraville Ranger Districts -- including Van Norden, the Donner Summit PCT Trailhead and Forest Road 80-051, all National Forest System land in California south of Hwy 80 and east of Hwy 89, the Hwy 89 South and Alpine Meadows areas, and the Little Truckee area (Prosser/Boca/Stampede country) -- with the only exceptions being Forest Service campgrounds, Forest Service designated dispersed campsites, and within 300 feet of the PCT or the Tahoe Rim Trail (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/tahoe/alerts/camping-and-campfire-restrictions-truckee-and-sierraville-districts). Tahoe NF is additionally under Stage 1 fire restrictions 2026-06-26 through 2026-10-31, which allow a gas/liquid-fuel stove or lantern only with a valid California Campfire Permit and only in a spot cleared 3 feet of flammable material (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/tahoe/alerts/stage-1-fire-restrictions-0). Tahoe NF also prohibits dispersed camping within roughly a quarter mile of major highway corridors in places -- check the Tahoe National Forest Visitor Map and the current forest order for the specific stretch you are on. CALIFORNIA SNO-PARKS: a permit is required for every vehicle parked at a SNO-PARK from November 1 through May 30 ($15/day or $40/season), displayed on the left side of the dashboard. Statewide rule: 'Overnight parking, including in-vehicle camping is allowed except where noted or signed', tent camping or sleeping outside the vehicle in the parking area is prohibited at every site, and vehicles parked overnight must be staked at all four corners with 1x2-inch by 8-foot poles (https://ohv.parks.ca.gov/?page_id=30701). Site-specific prohibitions exist and override that: the Donner Summit SNO-PARK explicitly prohibits camping and in-car camping by forest order, and Blackwood Canyon prohibits overnight camping. VOLATILITY: every order cited above expires, and fire restrictions are raised and lowered mid-season. Re-check https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/eldorado/alerts and https://www.fs.usda.gov/r05/tahoe/alerts before relying on any of this.

gaps.i-80-donner-summit-tahoe-nf: NO PINS SHIPPED for the I-80 / Donner Summit segment, deliberately. Everything within about 10 miles of Donner Summit that a low-clearance car can reach is either explicitly closed to camping or unverifiable: (1) Donner Summit SNO-PARK -- the obvious candidate, a plowed lot right on the corridor -- explicitly prohibits camping and in-car camping by forest order, per its own Forest Service page (https://fs.usda.gov/r05/tahoe/recreation/donner-summit-snowpark); (2) the Van Norden area and the Donner Summit PCT Trailhead / Forest Road 80-051 are named Restricted Use Areas under Forest Order 17-25-05, camping and fires both prohibited; (3) all NFS land in California south of I-80 and east of Hwy 89 is closed to camping under the same order, which removes the whole Truckee/Martis side; (4) the Little Truckee restricted area removes the Prosser / Boca / Stampede / Hwy 89 North country; (5) the dispersed areas that locals actually name for this corridor -- Grouse Ridge, Bowman Lake, Rucker Lake, Blue Lake, Sterling Lake via Rattlesnake Road, Foresthill Divide -- are all 5 to 15 miles of rough or steep dirt off Hwy 20 or a freeway exit, are described in their own sources as needing high clearance, and are snowbound roughly October through June. None of that is a Tesla Model Y at 11pm. This segment is already covered by legal, plowed, on-freeway options in caltrans-rest-areas.json (Donner Summit Safety Roadside Rest Area eastbound and westbound, Gold Run eastbound and westbound); those are the correct answer here and this category adds nothing safe to them.
gaps.us-50-ice-house-road-crystal-basin: Ice House Road (Forest Road 3) leaves US-50 about 23 miles east of Placerville and is paved for roughly the first 11 miles into the Crystal Basin -- on paper the best low-clearance-car dispersed corridor on this segment, and it is named as such by local sources. NO PIN SHIPPED because no defensible coordinate could be found: every source that names it describes it as 'drive up Ice House Road and find a spot' without a specific site, and dispersed camping is explicitly NOT allowed around Ice House Reservoir, Union Valley Reservoir, Wrights Lake or the other developed Crystal Basin sites, so a guessed coordinate has a real chance of landing somewhere posted closed. Worth a human field check.
gaps.iron-mountain-and-hwy-88: The abandoned Iron Mountain ski area on Hwy 88 is repeatedly described as flat, gravel-paved, car-accessible dispersed camping with SNO-PARK permit parking November to May. Excluded as off-corridor: it is not within 10 road miles of US-50, and the direct connection (Mormon Emigrant Trail, Forest Road 10N50) is closed to non-4WD passenger vehicles whenever snow covers it under Eldorado Forest Order 03-26-01 (2026-04-26 through 2028-04-25).
gaps.mvum-verification: None of the three shipped coordinates was checked against the Eldorado NF Motor Vehicle Use Map, which is the legal document of record for which roads have a designated dispersed-camping corridor and how wide it is (150 or 300 feet from centerline). That check needs the actual MVUM PDF for the Placerville and Pacific Ranger Districts and is the single highest-value follow-up for this category.

records.name: Echo Lake SNO-PARK (US-50, Echo Summit)
records.source: California State Parks OHMVR Division -- Echo Lake SNO-PARK
records.notes: Paved, plowed lot about half a mile in on Echo Lake Road / Johnson Pass Road, north side of US-50, roughly one mile west of Echo Summit, ~7,400 ft, Eldorado National Forest. ROAD: fully paved from US-50 -- a normal low-clearance car makes it, this is the only pin in this file that needs no dirt driving at all. SEASON: the one spot on this corridor that is BETTER in winter than in summer, because it is a plowed SNO-PARK. A California SNO-PARK permit is required for every vehicle November 1 through May 30 ($15/day or $40/season, displayed on the left dashboard; sold at the Kyburz Silverfork Store westbound and Sunrise Ski and Snowboard in South Lake Tahoe eastbound). Outside that window no permit is needed but it is just an unplowed Forest Service trailhead lot. WINTER CAVEAT: US-50 over Echo Summit is a chain-control and closure route -- the pin can be legal and still unreachable, and the state's own guidance is to avoid overnight parking here during active snow removal so you do not block a plow. There is no parking on the entry road (Johnson Pass Rd) itself. OVERNIGHT: permitted -- the statewide SNO-PARK rule is 'overnight parking, including in-vehicle camping is allowed except where noted or signed', and unlike Donner Summit and Blackwood Canyon this site carries no posted prohibition; the state page instead discusses how to park overnight here. Sleeping OUTSIDE the vehicle or pitching a tent in the lot is prohibited at all SNO-PARKs. Vehicles left overnight are supposed to be staked at all four corners with 1x2-inch by 8-foot poles. STAY LIMIT: 10 days per calendar year in the Eldorado's undeveloped locations (Forest Order 03-25-08). FIRE: as of 2026-08-12 Eldorado Forest Order 03-26-05 bans all flame outside listed developed sites including gas stoves and lanterns -- sleeping in the car is fine, cooking is not. CONFIDENCE: high on location (coordinate is the state's own, 38 deg 49' 26.63" N / 120 deg 2' 2.69" W) and high on legality of in-vehicle overnight use, since it rests on the published statewide SNO-PARK rule plus the absence of the site-specific ban that comparable sites do carry. Not personally visited; conditions, signage and the permit window can change.

records.name: Silver Fork Road dispersed area (US-50 at Kyburz)
records.source: The Dyrt (community) -- USFS Silver Fork Dispersed; area legality cross-checked against Eldorado NF official camping rules
records.notes: Dispersed camping corridor along Silver Fork Road, which leaves US-50 at Kyburz and follows the Silver Fork of the American River southeast, Eldorado National Forest, Placerville Ranger District, ~4,000-5,000 ft. The coordinate is the entrance to the area, roughly a mile up from US-50 -- NOT a specific site. ROAD: the lower road is a paved forest/county road; the actual camping is on dirt spurs off it, described by users as well-maintained but 'slightly tricky with a car' and likely bad after rain. For a low-clearance car the realistic play is to stay on the paved section and use a pullout within one vehicle length of the road edge, which is what the Eldorado's own rule requires anyway; do not commit to a dirt spur in the dark. SEASON: shoulder-season usable and one user reports camping here in December, but all dirt roads and trails on the Eldorado are closed to motor vehicles January 1 through March 31, and Silver Fork Road can hold snow and is not a priority plow route. Treat it as summer/early-fall only for a Model Y. BURN SCAR: this drainage burned in the 2021 Caldor Fire -- expect standing dead timber, and do not park under it in wind. STAY LIMIT: 10 days per calendar year in undeveloped locations per ranger district (Eldorado Forest Order 03-25-08). RULES: at least 100 ft from the creek, outside the marked boundary of Silver Fork and China Flat campgrounds, vehicle on a designated MVUM road. FIRE: as of 2026-08-12 all flame including gas stoves and lanterns is banned outside listed developed sites (Forest Order 03-26-05); when restrictions lift you still need a free California Campfire Permit. CONFIDENCE: medium-low. The area is named as a dispersed camping area by local sources and general dispersed camping here is consistent with Eldorado NF policy, but the coordinate is community-sourced and was not corroborated against the MVUM, and no specific legal site was confirmed. Some third-party listings claim a Recreation.gov permit is needed here -- that appears to be wrong; the Eldorado's own page says dispersed camping is free and permit-free apart from the campfire permit. Verify on the ground.

records.name: Packsaddle Pass Road dispersed area (US-50 near Strawberry)
records.source: The Dyrt (community) -- Packsaddle Pass, El Dorado National Forest Dispersed; area legality cross-checked against Eldorado NF official camping rules
records.notes: Dispersed camping on the ridge above Strawberry Valley, reached from US-50 near Strawberry / Twin Bridges, Eldorado National Forest, roughly 3-4 road miles off the highway and about 20 miles short of Echo Summit. ROAD: users describe a PAVED main road up the ridge with dirt spurs branching off to the sites, and it is a drive-in where you park next to your spot -- the best road profile of the two dispersed entries here for a low-clearance car, though one reviewer flags it as a bad idea after rain. SEASON: summer and early fall only in practice. This is a high ridge on the west side of Echo Summit; the spurs are unplowed and the Eldorado closes all dirt roads and trails to motor vehicles January 1 through March 31. Do not plan on this pin between roughly November and June. BURN SCAR AND LOGGING: reviewers note recent clearing and 'deforestation' with wide open cleared areas -- this is Caldor Fire salvage country, so expect exposure, dust, log trucks on weekdays, and dead standing timber. Some road noise from US-50 carries up. STAY LIMIT: 10 days per calendar year in undeveloped locations per ranger district (Eldorado Forest Order 03-25-08). RULES: 100 ft from water, outside developed campground boundaries, vehicle on a designated MVUM road and parked within one vehicle length of the road edge. FIRE: as of 2026-08-12 all flame including gas stoves and lanterns is banned outside listed developed sites (Forest Order 03-26-05); a free California Campfire Permit is required at other times. CONFIDENCE: medium-low. The coordinate is community-sourced and marks the area entrance, not a site; it was not corroborated against the Eldorado MVUM and no posted signage was verified. Dispersed camping in this general area is consistent with Eldorado NF policy and no closure order covers it as of 2026-08-12.
